utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-95-04-PT, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Gruban and Dusko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Joanna Korner together with Kapila Waidyaratne and Gina Butler as case manager. Can I just make an inquiry? Where is Mr. Gruban?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Senior legal officer. He's on provisional release. Yes. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Tom Moran for Mr. Knezevic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, representing Momcilo Gruban, Dudjer Milenko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a number of matters to go through. I'll go through my list and provide the information that I have. If any party wishes to raise an issue, then feel free to do so. Start first with pending motions, the motion for joinder with which we are familiar, and as I indicated in the earlier hearing, the Chamber will give a decision on this within the next two weeks. And there will be no oral hearing. There's a motion on the form of the indictment from Mr. Gruban. Again, that will have to await the determination of the joinder issue. The question of Mr. Knezevic's challenge to the assignment of counsel, that will be determined within the shortest possible time by the Chamber. We have a motion from Mr. Gruban for variation of conditions of provisional release. There was one issue that was brought to my attention relating to the copy of a guarantee from the Republika Srpska. There was some issue as to its authenticity, and the parties had been instructed to meet with the Registrar to determine whether the particular version could be filed, could probably be filed. May I ask whether that has been done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, it was filed yesterday, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was unaware of any instruction to meet with the Registrar. I'm unaware of any filing. But if I'm told there has been a filing, then fine.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, to clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think the Office of the Prosecutor is very large.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The instructions, I was to meet with the Defence counsel to arrange this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's what I thought, I don't think it went through the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Which I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Pretrial preparation, disclosure, witness statements, Rule 66 (A)(i) obligations on the part of the Prosecutor, my information is that 63 witness statements in total accompanied the indictment on confirmation, and all but one had been disclosed, both in English and B/C/S, within the required time frame. And that a final statement will be disclosed by Friday of this week. I am told, however, that the Defence have indicated that they are not aware of having received the material, and the Prosecution was checking this. Could you update me on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have been trying to get a hold of my secretary and have been unable to. The Prosecution said they sent to me by DHL a package containing what was it, 23 statements? 29 statements. And I just flat don't recall seeing it. If they say it's in my office, it's in my office. I have been trying to get a hold of my secretary to go through my desk and find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The sooner that can be clarified, the better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So if they have to be resent, which I hope that is not the case, then that can be done as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I have no doubt -- the last month frankly I have been clearing the decks and finishing up every other case I've got for this case. And I have been flipping through things and then setting them aside. So I would not be -- if they say it's there, it's there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a signed receipt, one of which was signed I think by this gentleman here on behalf of Defence counsel for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gruban.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Gruban, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was not signed by myself, but we have received it. The Prosecution has received it. 85 statements altogether issued by various witnesses. That would be Gruban's Defence. Nothing else, no other accompanying matter or material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I turn next to the obligations under Rule 66 (A)(ii) in respect of witness statements. The Prosecutor indicated that it would call approximately 23 witnesses in relation to Gruban, and 4 or 5 for Knezevic. And the Prosecution has agreed to provide the Defence and the Chamber with a chart detailing the statements that were included in the supporting material and identifying what material is new. Is that being done, or are you not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am. I'm aware of -- this happened yesterday at the 65 ter conference that was held. Your Honour, we can provide a chart of which witnesses were included in the original supporting material and so on. I think that's going to confuse matters something horrible, and it's in our submission unnecessary. We will provide a list of the witnesses that we're going to call. Whether they form part of the supporting material originally or whether they formed part of the additional material or whether they are new witnesses entirely, it seems isn't going to help much because one of the confusions that is going to arise as I can see from the note of the conference yesterday is which witnesses came where and how. In our submission, simply we will provide when we have decided a list of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Senior legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You'll be having another meeting with the senior legal officer, and the precise modalities for discharging that obligation can be elaborated there. Experts, the Prosecutor has identified one expert dealing with exhumations, and that report I understand is to be made available this week.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know where the "this week" came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm informed it will be provided to the Prosecutor this week.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm sure it will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Exhibits, no details of exhibits have yet been discussed. No new information on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Rule 68 material, no problems?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are conducting searches in respect of each defendant and in respect of the witnesses, but we're not in a position at the moment to disclose anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And reciprocal disclosure, that obligation has not been triggered. Rule 92 bis, which is to be utilised whenever it is feasible, the Prosecutor apparently is of the view that most of the evidence that it will adduce relates to the acts and conducts of the accused. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. But can I say, we're still in, from all parties' side, in the early stages in this case. And matters are complicated by the fact that the appeal in the original trial is pending. It may well be, particularly -- I'm not sure there's a date for that appeal, but once that appeal is resolved, that we will be able to reduce substantially the way in which evidence is presented. In particular, by motions seeking the recognition of adjudicated facts. I don't anticipate, and I may be wrong, that this case is likely to come to trial before the end of this year from what I know of the Court listings. And we would hope that by the time the case does come to trial the appeal will be resolved, and that may shorten matters quite substantially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. Well, my next item I think you have touched on, agreed facts and adjudicated facts. Perhaps not agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I mean, Your Honour, as I say, I think what we may be able to achieve certainly well before trial is some kind of agreement as to facts which will not be in dispute. I hope now we have reached the position both in this case and although it wasn't mentioned, in the Keraterm case where what will be at issue during the trial is what was the conduct and the acts of the accused and not much else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I encourage the parties to work together. The filing of the pre-trial brief, again, this is a matter that will be influenced by the decision on joinder. But I would give, in an indicative way, the same dates that I gave in the earlier hearing, that is, assuming that the decision is given on joinder within two weeks, then the OTP would have two months after joinder, taking them some time into mid-November, and the Defence one month, towards the end of January. However, the definitive dates will be set after the joinder decision. The length of trial, I believe the OTP had indicated that a trial relating to Gruban and Knezevic would probably take three to four months in chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, all of this is dependent on so many factors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If it's two accused, I would estimate that it will certainly be three months for the Prosecution's case, at the minimum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The date of the next Status Conference, again, this might be influenced by the joinder decision. But the date that I would fix is Monday, the 16th of December. Before I call on the accused, is there any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one short matter. The Court has already touched on this, on the matter of Mr. Knezevic's counsel, both in this case and the other case. The Court's already said that we're going to have a ruling soon. Just so that the Court understands the problem I'm operating under, there is a limited amount of resources that have been budgeted for his Defence. And if I do a lot of work, and then am replaced, the replacement counsel won't have those resources available, either time or money. The other side of the coin is we're running out of time. So we need a decision that the Court can live with, I can live with, Mr. Knezevic can live with, as quickly as possible, Your Honour, to protect his rights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And... Mr. Knezevic, is there anything you'd like to say? I was asking Mr. Knezevic whether there was any matter you'd want to raise at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes I do. I've already said 20 minutes ago that I don't wish Mr. Moran to represent me before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We've already heard that submission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any other matter? There being none, the hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
